input.summary:
Implemented a Task Management API in TypeScript following the provided contracts and architecture rules. Key components:

- src/types.ts: All shared data models, event bus contract, event payloads, and service interfaces.
- src/event-bus.ts: EventBus implementing IEventBus with in-memory subscribers.
- Services (one per file, no cross-service imports, own private data stores, no HTTP):
  - src/services/user-service.ts (IUserService)
  - src/services/project-service.ts (IProjectService)
  - src/services/task-service.ts (ITaskService) — enforces forward-only status transitions and publishes task events.
  - src/services/comment-service.ts (ICommentService) — publishes comment.added events.
  - src/services/notification-service.ts (INotificationService) — subscribes to events and creates notifications using lookup helpers.
- src/router.ts: HTTP-only router using Node’s http module, mapping all routes to services, handling JSON bodies and errors.
- src/main.ts: Wires up EventBus, services, notification subscriptions, creates and starts the HTTP server (default port 3000).
- src/demo.ts: Demo script that spins up a server on port 3001 and exercises end-to-end flow: create users, create project, add members, create tasks, assign, change status, add comments, view and mark notifications.
- tsconfig.json configured for strict TypeScript compilation. tsc not available in environment, but runtime verified via tsx.

Validation:
- Ran demo: npx tsx src/demo.ts — server started on 3001 and demonstrated all features with proper notifications.
- Event wiring: NotificationService subscribes to task.assigned, task.statusChanged, and comment.added; TaskService and CommentService publish as required.
- Architecture rules obeyed: no cross-service imports, exclusive data stores, no HTTP in services, forward-only status transitions, no external packages, one service per file.

To run:
- Start server: npx tsx src/main.ts (defaults to port 3000)
- Run demo: npx tsx src/demo.ts
